subject: research/sequential-slashing
professional: a sequential-analysis statistician (anytime-valid inference / e-values) refereeing for a statistics or crypto-economics venue; they would check first that the false-slash guarantee is exact, that the mixture e-process is valid, and what is new relative to Ville, Wald, Robbins and the forecast-calibration literature

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (9.97 s): output is byte-identical to experiments/results.txt (diff SAME). Recomputed independently with an exact dynamic program over (successes, t) that shares no code with model.py (script outside the repo): (1) KL(0.3||0.2)=0.028168 and Wald ln(20)/KL=106.35, matching the reported 0.0282 and 106; (2) exact false-slash probability of the peeking z-test (t0=30, T=2000, p=0.2, alpha=0.05) = 0.3731 vs reported 0.371 (Monte Carlo, 2000 trials); (3) exact LR e-process false-slash probability = 0.0432 (<= 0.05 as Ville requires) vs reported 0.038 (1.1 SE away, consistent); (4) exact mean detection time of the oracle LR at q=0.3 = 111.8 (detect prob 1.0) vs reported 119 (E2, 600 trials, about 1.7 SE), 108 (E3) and 112 (E4): consistent within noise but the true overshoot over Wald is 5%, not the 12% quoted. (5) Mixture false-slash rate re-run with 1500 trials, seed 99, K=32: 0.0253 vs reported 0.020 (300 trials): within the +/-1.6pp interval of the original. No number was wrong; the sampling error is just never reported.
evidence.completeness: README and whitepaper claim R1 (peeking inflation vs Ville), R2 (delay vs Wald, log in 1/alpha, 1/KL effect-size scaling), R3 (price of ignorance) and a 6-test suite; all work end to end: tests run (6 OK in 0.26 s), results reproduce, E1-E4 each produce the cited figure, delay_vs_alpha.svg and experiments/figure.py exist (figure content not inspected). No stubs or TODOs in the 99-line module. Gaps are things the note itself lists as out of scope (time-varying p_t, adaptive adversary, stake model). The project has no project.json (card lives in _homepage/projects.json) and is not listed in PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 6 tests, OK. Mutation 1 (drop the /K in run_mixture's log-mean, which makes the mixture e-process invalid, false-slash rate 0.35 at K=16, T=2000, 300 trials): 1 test failed, but only test_mixture_detects_slower_than_oracle (the mutant detects faster than the oracle), by accident; no test checks the mixture's false-slash rate or its mean-one property as a process. Mutation 2 (LR threshold lowered from ln(1/alpha) to ln(1/(2 alpha))): 2 tests failed (Ville and Wald). Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean. Weaknesses: the Ville test is 800 trials at alpha=0.1 with +0.03 slack, the peeking test only asserts >0.15, no test for z-test correctness, edge inputs, or run_ztest_peeking/run_lr return values on a fixed sequence. Validity of the headline mixture method is effectively untested.
evidence.craft: Read src/sequential_slashing/model.py (99 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, paper/whitepaper.md. Readable, stdlib-only, documented functions. Defects: no input validation (p or q of 0 or 1 raises ZeroDivisionError or math domain error inside kl/lr_step; q<=p is silently accepted by run_lr, which would then never slash honest-or-not); false_slash_rate treats any unknown method string as 'lr' (silent fallback) and then KeyErrors on kw['q']; run_mixture recomputes K logs per step (O(TK) pure Python, 300 trials max in experiments) and re-imports NormalDist inside the function; the draw is materialised for the full T even when the rule stops at t=60; `from .model import *` with __all__ re-export in the package; tests and experiments hard-code sys.path manipulation; K differs by caller (64 default, 32 in run.py, 16 and 8 in tests) without comment; no CI-style statistical error bars in run.py output.
evidence.claims: Backed by files: README headline numbers (37%, 3.8%, 2.0%, x1.36) equal results.txt, which reproduces exactly; '6 tests' and '~10 s' are true; Ville inequality statement is correct. Not backed or overstated: (a) 'connecting to Frongillo-Waggoner-style proper scoring: the betting factor is a (shifted) score' is asserted with no derivation or citation (no reference list at all, only author-year names); (b) 'detection delay tracks Wald's bound to within 12%': exact overshoot at q=0.3 is 5%, and 9 vs 8 at q=0.6 is 12.5% on the rounded values, so the figure is noise-dependent and quoted without intervals; (c) 'attains Wald's bound up to overshoot' is presented as a finding, but for an LR e-process E[tau]=E[ln E_tau]/KL >= ln(1/alpha)/KL is Wald's identity, so it is a consequence, not an experiment; (d) 'any level-alpha test' bound is stated without the power term, only partly caveated in Limits; (e) E1 mixture rate is from 300 trials and 2.0% carries about +/-1.6pp; (f) labelled 'Stylised' with all inputs (p=0.2, q in {0.25..0.6}) round numbers and no sweep over p, though research/CLAUDE.md asks for sourced or swept parameters. Limits section is honest and there is a 'no claims about any deployed protocol' disclaimer.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? Partly. The code is small enough to fork and the experiments are reproducible, but the result is a textbook application: Ville (1939) and Wald (1945) give the guarantee and the delay, Robbins (1970) the mixture method, Shafer-Vovk testing-by-betting and Ramdas et al. (2023, cited by name) the e-process framing. Nearest prior work on this exact question (is a probability forecaster calibrated, tested sequentially) is Arnold, Henzi and Ziegel, 'Sequentially valid tests for forecast calibration', and Choe and Ramdas, 'Comparing sequential forecasters'; also Waudby-Smith and Ramdas on betting for bounded means. None is cited (cited from memory by this auditor, bibliographic details not verified). The note claims no novelty over them and does not position itself. The protocol-specific contribution (staked slashing, price of deterrence) is a three-line implication with no model. The library handles a constant known p only, whereas a verifier's reports vary per round, so the object a researcher would actually need (e-process for time-varying forecasts p_t, composite alternatives, confidence sequence for the fault rate) is absent. Not packaged for reuse beyond a pyproject. Not part of a programme in PROGRAMMES.md, so well below the PhD+ aim in research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard anytime-valid inference practice (Howard et al. 2021, Ramdas et al. 2023, Waudby-Smith and Ramdas 2024). A referee would accept the LR e-process and the Ville argument. Departures: the mixture is uniform over the betting fraction lambda in (0,1/p), not the conjugate Beta mixture over q used by Robbins and the literature (and not a predictable plug-in/ONS bet), with no argument for the choice and no regret bound beyond the 'about half ln n' remark; the null is a single known p rather than a composite, time-varying forecast; one-sided only (over-reporting faults is not tested); no power calculation beyond mean delay; simulations at only p=0.2 (a verifier fault probability near 1% or lower would stress the z-test and lattice effects very differently); no treatment of the adversary choosing when to deviate, which is the actual economic attack on slashing. A crypto-economics reviewer would additionally want a stake and deterrence model, which is absent.

defects.what: No test checks validity of the mixture e-process (false-slash rate or mean-one product). Seeded mutation that drops the /K normaliser (false-slash rate 0.35 instead of <=0.05) was caught only incidentally by a detection-delay ordering test.

Whitepaper cites Frongillo-Waggoner proper scoring, Ville, Shafer-Vovk and Ramdas et al. by name only (no reference list), omits the closest prior work on sequential forecast-calibration testing (Arnold-Henzi-Ziegel; Choe-Ramdas) and states no novelty claim.
Library supports only a constant known p. A verifier reporting varying probabilities p_t, the stated motivation, cannot be tested; one-sided only; no composite alternative or confidence sequence.

Simulated numbers quoted without Monte Carlo error. Exact oracle-LR mean delay at q=0.3 is 111.8 (overshoot 5% over Wald); the project reports 119, 108 and 112 for the same setting and quotes 'within 12%'. Mixture false-slash 0.020 rests on 300 trials (re-run with 1500: 0.025).
Tightness of the LR delay to Wald is presented as an empirical result but follows from Wald's identity; the 'any level-alpha test' bound is quoted without its power term.
No input validation; q<=p silently accepted by run_lr; unknown method string silently falls back to LR then KeyErrors on q; p in {0,1} crashes in kl/lr_step.
All inputs are round numbers at a single p=0.2 and the project is labelled Stylised; no sweep over p or sourced verifier fault rates as research/CLAUDE.md asks.
Ville and peeking tests have loose thresholds (alpha+0.03 slack, >0.15) and a single seed, so a modest invalidity would pass.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible stdlib note: the project does what it says (6 tests pass, run.py reproduces results.txt byte for byte), and its headline numbers survive an exact dynamic-programming recomputation (peeking z-test false-slash 0.373 exact vs 0.371 reported; LR e-process 0.043 exact vs 0.038, within Monte Carlo error and under the 0.05 Ville bound; oracle delay 111.8 exact vs 108 to 119 reported). So it is correct and finished. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 because a seeded invalidating mutation in the mixture e-process was caught only by an incidental test, and claims is 2 because of an asserted but undeveloped Frongillo-Waggoner link, no reference list, 'within 12%' quoted from noisy means, and an unstated novelty position. The deeper limit is fitness and domain: the result is a textbook application of Ville, Wald and Robbins to a constant known p, it omits the nearest prior work on sequential calibration testing, and it lacks the time-varying forecast case and stake model that would make it a researcher's starting point. Cheapest improvements: add a mixture false-slash test, add Monte Carlo intervals and a reference list naming the prior work, and extend the e-process to p_t.
